sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Arvalus was an obscure Continental Celtic god of healing. The invading Romans equated him with Apollo. The Romans used the name Apollo for divinities of thermal springs. Arvalus may once have ruled such a shrine. Roman writers recorded little about him. Modern scholars know few details of his cult. His association with Apollo points to a healing and water god. The shrines he guarded drew pilgrims who sought cures. Such warm spring sanctuaries held great importance in the Roman world. The equation helped Romans fit a local god into their own pantheon.
